title: Referee observer charged over alleged language referencing ‘race, ethnic origin or nationality’
content:
A referee match observer is facing potential action from the Football Association after allegedly using “abusive or insulting” language with reference to “race, ethnic origin or nationality” before a League One fixture.

Brian Curson, a former English Football League referee, has been charged with a breach of FA rules after alleged misconduct before November’s League One fixture between Luton Town and Rotherham United.

The FA confirmed in a statement on Wednesday that it was alleged Curson had “acted in an improper manner and/or used abusive and/or insulting words” before the game. This could constitute an aggravated breach of the FA’s rules, as it allegedly “included a reference, whether express or implied, to ethnic origin and/or race and/or nationality”.

A referee match observer is appointed to games to assess officials and provide a report on their performance. The FA typically sanctions individual players, managers, coaches and backroom staff for alleged breaches of its misconduct rules, while clubs are also disciplined for fan or player behaviour en masse, and it is highly unusual for a referee match observer to be charged by the governing body.

Curson has until May 8 to provide a response.

The League One fixture between Luton and Rotherham took place on November 15 at Kenilworth Road, and finished in a 0-0 draw.
